core.pose.rest — layout grammar v1
==================================

Magic "WKRP" (57 4B 52 50), envelope version 1.
Read spec/layouts/ENVELOPE.layout.txt first.

What it is
----------
The set of orientations in which this entity comes to rest when dropped on a
flat, level, infinitely rigid floor — measured, not guessed, by dropping the
entity in a rigid-body simulation from many random initial orientations and
recording where it settles. The profile's target count is 32 distinct
settled orientations, but the count is whatever the measurement found and is
declared in the header.

Each entry carries the orientation, how often the drop sim landed there, and
the contact points that touch the floor in that orientation.

Two masters (law 9): a runtime uses it to place props convincingly without
simulating; the tooling uses the contact points to pick a thumbnail camera
that does not shoot the object from underneath, and to place the object in
imposter bakes.

Header keys (in addition to the mandatory envelope keys)
--------------------------------------------------------

  key                type            meaning
  -----------------  --------------  --------------------------------------
  "pose_count"       uint            number of entries in section 0.
  "contact_count"    uint            total number of contact points in
                                     section 1, summed over all entries.
  "trials"           uint            how many drops were simulated. 0 means
                                     the poses were authored, not measured;
                                     "probability" is then meaningless and
                                     MUST be 0.0 in every entry.
  "floor_normal"     array<float>[3] model-space direction the floor normal
                                     points, unit. Canonically [0,1,0] (the
                                     manifest's up_axis).
  "settle_epsilon_m" float           the linear tolerance the sim used to
                                     declare "settled", metres.
  "merge_angle_deg"  float           two settled orientations closer than
                                     this angle were merged into one entry;
                                     their probabilities were summed.

Payload sections
----------------

  section 0
    "name"   : "poses"
    "dtype"  : "record"
    "shape"  : [pose_count]
    "stride" : 32
    "size"   : 32 * pose_count

    record layout, 32 bytes, little-endian, no implicit padding:

      offset  size  type   field
      ------  ----  -----  --------------------------------------------
       +0      4    f32    quat_w
       +4      4    f32    quat_x
       +8      4    f32    quat_y
      +12      4    f32    quat_z     (order is w,x,y,z; see conventions)
      +16      4    u32    contact_first  index of this entry's first
                                          contact point in section 1
      +20      4    u32    contact_count  number of contact points, >= 1
      +24      4    f32    probability    fraction of trials that settled
                                          here, 0.0..1.0
      +28      4    f32    support_area_m2  area of the convex hull of this
                                          entry's contact points projected
                                          onto the floor plane, m^2. 0.0 if
                                          fewer than 3 contacts.

    The quaternion rotates the entity FROM its model-space rest orientation
    INTO the settled orientation, in the manifest's declared handedness. To
    place a settled instance: R = quat, then translate so the lowest contact
    point sits on the floor plane.

    Invariant a reader MUST check:
      sum over entries of contact_count == header "contact_count"
      entries are sorted by "probability" DESCENDING; entry 0 is the most
      likely resting pose and is what a tool uses when it needs exactly one.
      sum of probability over all entries is 1.0 +/- 1e-3 when trials > 0.

  section 1
    "name"   : "contacts"
    "dtype"  : "f32"
    "shape"  : [contact_count, 3]
    "stride" : 12
    "size"   : 12 * contact_count

    Contact point c, components (x,y,z), lives at
        offset + 12*c + 0, +4, +8
    Coordinates are in MODEL space (the entity's own untransformed frame),
    metres — NOT in the settled frame. To get floor-space positions, apply
    the entry's quaternion. Storing them in model space means one point can
    be shared conceptually across poses and lets a reader show contact
    points on the untransformed mesh without inverting anything.

Decisions recorded here
-----------------------
  D-RP-1  Two sections with fixed strides, rather than the variable-length
          "count then that many points, then the next entry" record the
          draft sketched. Variable-length records force a reader to DERIVE
          each entry's offset by walking the file, which law 8's corollary
          forbids. With a fixed 32-byte entry stride plus an index into a
          flat contact array, entry N is at a computed-from-declared-stride
          offset and can be read with one numpy view.
  D-RP-2  "up_contact_count" from the draft is named "contact_count" here.
          There is no separate notion of an up-contact: a contact point is a
          point that touches the floor, and which way is up is stated once,
          in "floor_normal".
  D-RP-3  Contacts are in model space, not settled space (rationale above).
  D-RP-4  probability is stored per entry rather than a raw hit count, so
          the field remains meaningful after entries are merged or pruned.
          "trials" is kept so a consumer can recover counts and judge the
          statistical weight of a small probability.
  D-RP-5  Entries are sorted by probability descending, normatively. A
          consumer that wants "the" rest pose reads entry 0 and needs no
          policy of its own.
